stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that was promised a certificate
The group that drew without a reward

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

columns.label: Mean score on the final test (%)

rows.group: The group that took practice quizzes
The group that reread the passage

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They hypothesized that the amount of sleep would affect reaction time.

**Participants.** The sample was 60 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

**Results.** The group that stayed awake all night: mean reaction time (ms) = 412. The group that slept for eight hours: mean reaction time (ms) = 318. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.why: A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This is the independent variable.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes histrionic personality disorder?

options.text: The personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking
options.why: Correct. This is what histrionic personality disorder means.

options.text: The personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact
options.why: That describes avoidant personality disorder.

options.text: The personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others
options.why: That describes antisocial personality disorder.

options.text: The personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior
options.why: That describes borderline personality disorder.

questions.explanation: Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a lobotomy?

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: Correct. This is what a lobotomy means.

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: That describes electroconvulsive therapy.

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: That describes transcranial magnetic stimulation.

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes psychotropic medication.

questions.explanation: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing?

options.why: The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
Correct. The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.explanation: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.stem: The more hours children spend reading, the larger their vocabularies tend to be. Which kind of relationship is this?

options.why: The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
Correct. A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones?

options.why: The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
Correct. A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.explanation: A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that age causes a change in score on a timed reasoning test?

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: On a very easy test, most students score near 100 but a few score very low, so the mean is below the median. Which shape does the distribution have?

options.why: A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.
The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.
A positive skew is a distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median.
Correct. A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.explanation: A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: The meditation group had lower cortisol levels. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The daily activity and stress are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The daily activity caused the difference in stress
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a token economy?

options.text: The technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them
options.why: That describes biofeedback.

options.text: The behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards
options.why: Correct. This is what a token economy means.

options.text: The use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones
options.why: That describes applied behavior analysis.

options.text: The exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli
options.why: That describes systematic desensitization.

questions.explanation: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions?

options.why: Correct. A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.

questions.explanation: A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.stem: Athletes perform poorly when they are either too relaxed or too anxious, and best when moderately excited. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
Correct. The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes normative social influence?

options.text: Persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker
options.why: That describes the peripheral route to persuasion.

options.text: A rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group
options.why: That describes a social norm.

options.text: Persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully
options.why: That describes the central route to persuasion.

options.text: The influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection
options.why: Correct. This is what normative social influence means.

questions.explanation: Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the smallest unit of language that carries meaning?

options.why: Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.
Correct. A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.

questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: The inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life
options.why: That describes infantile amnesia.

options.text: The inability to form new memories after an injury or illness
options.why: That describes anterograde amnesia.

options.text: The loss of memories from before an injury or illness
options.why: That describes retrograde amnesia.

options.text: A progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities
options.why: Correct. This is what Alzheimer's disease means.

questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.stem: Scores on the odd-numbered questions of a test closely match scores on the even-numbered questions. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Correct. Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.
Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.explanation: Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group creativity, curiosity, judgment and love of learning under which virtue?

options.why: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Correct. Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.

questions.explanation: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter is the main excitatory messenger in the brain, with too much of it able to overstimulate the brain and trigger seizures?

options.why: Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.
Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter that enables muscle movement, learning and memory.
Correct. Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.
Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.

questions.explanation: Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a mood stabilizer that levels out the highs and lows of a patient with bipolar disorder. Which drug is this most likely to be?

options.why: An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
Correct. Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.explanation: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.stem: A tumor just above the ear disrupts a patient's ability to process sounds. Which lobes are affected?

options.why: The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.
The motor cortex is the strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.
The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.
Correct. The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.

questions.explanation: The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative?

options.why: Correct. Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.

questions.explanation: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.stem: Marc reads the assigned novel only because he wants a good grade. Which kind of motivation is this?

options.why: An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
Correct. Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.stem: A dog already salivates to a tone. A light is then repeatedly shown just before the tone, and the dog begins to salivate to the light. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Correct. Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.explanation: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: A one-year-old says 'milk' to mean 'I want some milk'. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
Correct. The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.explanation: The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.stem: A patient stands rigid in one position for several hours and does not respond to anyone. Which symptom is this?

options.why: A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them?

options.why: Correct. A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.
The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.explanation: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.

questions.stem: A two-year-old insists, 'Me do it!' when getting dressed. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Correct. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being?

options.why: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
Correct. An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.

questions.explanation: An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The number of times that each child raised a hand during one week
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This is the independent variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: Each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: During deep sleep, the body releases growth hormone and repairs muscle tissue. This best supports which function of sleep?

options.why: The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
Correct. Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: To finish a long project, Nia sets goals, makes a schedule, resists distractions and checks her progress. These skills are examples of which of the following?

options.why: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.
Correct. Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.

questions.explanation: Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.

questions.stem: After a stroke, Mr. Lee understands what people say but can only produce slow, broken speech. Which area was most likely damaged?

options.why: Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Correct. Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.explanation: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes object permanence?

options.text: The understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight
options.why: Correct. This is what object permanence means.

options.text: The understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes
options.why: That describes conservation.

options.text: The understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state
options.why: That describes reversibility.

options.text: The understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings
options.why: That describes theory of mind.

questions.explanation: Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.

questions.stem: Maya decides to raise her hand in class, and her arm muscles respond. Which part of the nervous system carries out this voluntary movement?

options.why: The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.
The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
Correct. The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes?

options.why: Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Correct. Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.explanation: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.stem: A therapist keeps a client's records confidential and lets the client decide whether to continue treatment. Which ethical principle is he following?

options.why: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.
Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Correct. Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.explanation: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.

questions.stem: Six dots are drawn as three close pairs, and people see three groups rather than six dots. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Correct. Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.explanation: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sublimation?

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: That describes regression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: Correct. This is what sublimation means.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron contains the nucleus?

options.why: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
Correct. The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.

questions.explanation: The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.

questions.stem: At thirteen months, Ella takes her first steps. Walking is an example of which of the following?

options.why: A critical period is a limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development.
Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.
Correct. Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.

questions.explanation: Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.

questions.stem: Hallucinations and delusions are experiences that are present in schizophrenia but absent in healthy functioning. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: Correct. A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.explanation: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.

questions.stem: After a stroke, a man can describe a person's nose and eyes but cannot recognize his own wife's face. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Correct. Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.

questions.explanation: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that optimism score causes a change in the number of days of illness in a year?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: Avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Correct. Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.explanation: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true?

options.why: Correct. A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.
Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.

questions.explanation: A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.

questions.stem: A survey asks people to rate their happiness and their satisfaction with life on a scale of 1 to 10. What is the survey measuring?

options.why: Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.
Correct. Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.explanation: Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it?

options.why: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.
Correct. REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.explanation: REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler approaches her mother, then freezes, then backs away with a dazed expression. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.
Correct. Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.
Anxious attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion.
Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.

questions.explanation: Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: The caffeine group detected more targets. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Caffeine and attention are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: Caffeine caused the difference in attention
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: While chatting at a crowded party, Deshawn suddenly notices his own name spoken across the room. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.

questions.stem: Before collecting any data, a researcher must have her plan approved by a university committee that checks its ethics. What is this committee called?

options.why: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.
Correct. An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.stem: Omar generally feels that he is a valuable and likeable person. Which term describes this overall feeling?

options.why: Correct. Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.
Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.

questions.explanation: Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.stem: Aaron spends his weekends skydiving and rock climbing. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Correct. Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress?

options.why: Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: Which receptor cells let a person see the colors and fine details of a painting in daylight?

options.why: Correct. Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.
The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.
Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.

questions.explanation: Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes stereotype lift?

options.text: The worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance
options.why: That describes stereotype threat.

options.text: A test that measures what a person has already learned
options.why: That describes an achievement test.

options.text: The boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped
options.why: Correct. This is what stereotype lift means.

options.text: The belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning
options.why: That describes a growth mindset.

questions.explanation: Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 8, 8, 4, 21, 7, 10, 12. What is the median of the scores?

options.why: Correct. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven.
That is the mean.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 4, 7, 8, 8, 10, 12, 21. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven. The one very high score pulls the mean (10) above the median (8), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory?

options.why: Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Correct. Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions?

options.why: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Correct. Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.explanation: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.stem: Which memory store holds a person's childhood memories and vocabulary for decades?

options.why: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Correct. Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.
Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.explanation: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience?

options.why: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.
The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Correct. The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.

questions.explanation: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.stem: A psychologist says a client's phobia was learned when a dog bite was paired with fear, and is kept going because avoiding dogs brings relief. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The evolutionary perspective is the view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful.
The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.
The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.
Correct. The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.

questions.explanation: The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.

questions.stem: At seventy, Mr. Park is slower than he used to be at solving unfamiliar logic puzzles. Which kind of intelligence has declined?

options.why: Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Correct. Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.

questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination?

options.why: Correct. Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.
Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.

questions.explanation: Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The number of other people present
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Raccoons trained to drop coins into a box began rubbing the coins together as if washing food, despite getting no reward for it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.
A primary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as food or water, that satisfies a biological need and is rewarding without learning.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.explanation: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of reaction time

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of reaction time.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Reaction time was defined as the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. On average, the value was 412 for the group that stayed awake all night and 318 for the group that slept for eight hours, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 60 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. (412 compared with 318).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the amount of sleep affects reaction time. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the amount of sleep. The finding illustrates sleep restores the brain, so sleep loss impairs attention and reaction time.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
